experiment: Phase 6.5 - live safety monitor overhead benchmark

config.prompt: The best way to deal with a difficult situation is
config.trial_order: Counterbalanced across 3 rotating orderings of {baseline, naive_monitor, optimized_monitor} to control for thermal/background drift
config.monitor_timing: One-token-delayed: first step scores the final prompt token; final generated token is not scored
config.sanity_check: All three conditions verified to generate byte-identical output on every trial (monitoring does not alter generation)

baseline.description: One forward pass per token, no monitoring

naive_full_sae_monitor.description: One forward pass per token plus a full SAE forward (all 8192 encoder features + full decoder reconstruction)

optimized_monitor.description: One forward pass per token, computing only the 100 selected encoder features directly (no full SAE encode, no decoder)

finding: The optimized one-pass monitoring kernel added a mean of +0.66% overhead, with a 95% confidence interval spanning zero - not statistically distinguishable from no overhead at all. The naive full-SAE implementation added a real, statistically distinguishable +4.12% overhead. Computing only the required 100 encoder features (skipping the decoder and 8,092 unused features) eliminated approximately 84% of the naive implementation's measured overhead.
limitations: CPU-only, 4 threads, no KV-caching; absolute numbers and relative overhead may differ on GPU or in a KV-cached production serving engine

This result applies to the optimized benchmark kernel specifically; the deployed /safety/monitor API endpoint currently uses a separate, correctness-first two-pass implementation and has not yet adopted this optimization
